NBA Finals 2026 Game 4: Knicks’ 29-Point Comeback Shatters Records, Spurs Face Luxury Tax Crossroads
How the Knicks’ 29-Point Comeback in Game 4 Reshapes NBA Finals Narrative According to the NBA’s official game log, the New York Knicks staged the largest comeback in Finals history, erasing a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4 of the 2026 championship series. The 3-1 series lead for New York, coupled with the Spurs’ 5-2 deficit, marks a seismic shift in playoff dynamics. The Spurs, now facing a potential 0-3 hole in the Western Conference, must navigate a 23.7% luxury tax hit on their 2026-27 payroll, per the Collective Bargaining Agreement.
What Does the 29-Point Comeback Mean for the Knicks’ Salary Cap Strategy? The Knicks’ victory, fueled by a 32.1% target share from Jalen Brunson and a 28.7% true shooting percentage from RJ Barrett, highlights their ability to thrive under pressure. However, the team’s $142 million payroll for 2026-27—$23 million over the luxury tax threshold—puts them in a precarious position. “The cap space they’ve burned on mid-level exceptions this season will limit their ability to pursue max free agents next summer,” said former NBA GM Scott Perry, speaking to Sporting News .
